root_cause.text: The stmmac GMAC4 split-header RX path in stmmac_rx_buf2_len() incorrectly assumed every non-last descriptor had a fully filled buf2 of dma_buf_sz, instead of using the RDES3 PL field, causing miscomputed buf2 lengths and invalid DMA sync/access in subsequent descriptors.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the non-last-descriptor fast path from unconditional `if (status & rx_not_ls) return priv->dma_conf.dma_buf_sz;` to only apply for non-GMAC4, and for GMAC4 uses `plen = stmmac_get_rx_frame_len(...); return plen - len;`; the commit/CVE explicitly states that on GMAC4 "the hardware does not fill buf2 of the first descriptor with payload" in rare cases, so assuming buf2 is fully filled "will be calculated wrong and cause an oops."

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes the non-last-descriptor fast path from unconditional `if (status & rx_not_ls) return priv->dma_conf.dma_buf_sz;` to only apply for non-GMAC4, and for GMAC4 uses `plen = stmmac_get_rx_frame_len(...); return plen - len;`; the commit/CVE explicitly states that on GMAC4 "the hardware does not fill buf2 of the first descriptor with payload" in rare cases, so assuming buf2 is fully filled "will be calculated wrong and cause an oops."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix GMAC4 split-header RX buf2 length calculation by using transferred packet length instead of assuming non-last descriptors always fill buf2.
intent_record.what: The function stmmac_rx_buf2_len() was changed to stop unconditionally returning dma_buf_sz for every non-last RX descriptor when split header is active. A detailed comment was added explaining a GMAC4-specific hardware case, the condition was narrowed from `if (status & rx_not_ls)` to `if (priv->plat->core_type != DWMAC_CORE_GMAC4 && (status & rx_not_ls))`, and the code now computes `plen = stmmac_get_rx_frame_len(...)` and returns `plen - len` for GMAC4 descriptors as well as for last descriptors.
intent_record.how: At runtime, non-last descriptors on non-GMAC4 cores still assume buf2 is fully filled, but GMAC4 no longer makes that assumption. For GMAC4, buf2 length is derived from the reported transferred-byte count instead of always using the full DMA buffer size, which avoids miscalculating the second buffer length in rare split-header receive cases and prevents a resulting kernel oops.

grouping_result.intent: Fix GMAC4 split-header RX buf2 length calculation by using transferred packet length instead of assuming non-last descriptors always fill buf2.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes GMAC4 split-header RX buf2 length computation by using the actual transferred packet length/RDES3 PL semantics instead of assuming non-last descriptors always use full dma_buf_sz, addressing the incorrect DMA sync/access issue.

candidates.rationale: This unconditional return for every non-last split-header RX descriptor embodies the faulty assumption that buf2 is always fully filled to dma_buf_sz. The root cause states buf2 length should instead be derived from the actual transferred packet length (RDES3 PL), so this statement directly causes the miscomputed buf2 length and subsequent invalid DMA sync/access.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement is the faulty non-last-descriptor return path in stmmac_rx_buf2_len() that unconditionally assumes buf2 is filled to dma_buf_sz. For GMAC4 split-header RX, buf2 length must be computed from the actual packet length indicated by the descriptor PL field; returning dma_buf_sz here miscomputes the DMA length and leads to invalid DMA sync/access on subsequent descriptors.

The vulnerability root cause is that in the GMAC4 split-header RX path, buf2 length was computed by assuming every non-last descriptor uses a full `dma_buf_sz` instead of using the descriptor payload length (`RDES3 PL`). bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body is sufficient because it contains the RX split-packet accumulation logic and the exact buf2 length assumption relevant to the root cause. The vulnerable construct is present in the multi-descriptor path: when a packet is not last-segment, the code does `len += priv->dma_buf_sz;` and later, for appended fragments, `if (likely(status & rx_not_ls)) buf_len = priv->dma_buf_sz;`. The root cause states the bug is that split-header RX in `stmmac_rx_buf2_len()` assumed every non-last descriptor had a fully filled buf2 of `dma_buf_sz` instead of using RDES3 PL; this function shows the same faulty assumption directly in the RX assembly logic for subsequent descriptors.
